q: A takeover of housing stock is defended by invoking the directive shield. What is the first question to ask?
options: Whether the law gives effect to one of the two shielded directives
Whether the State has obtained the prior concurrence of Parliament
Whether the owners were heard before the law was introduced
Whether the shield has been invoked expressly in the preamble of the law
expl: The shield is confined to two directives; that threshold decides everything else.
why: The remaining options describe procedural steps that sound plausible but form no part of the shield's operation.
trapnote: Test the threshold before the merits. If the law is outside the two clauses, nothing else matters.

q: A note states that the 2024 ruling made all private property a community resource. What kind of error is this?
options: An overstatement: the ruling so held, subject to payment of compensation
An omission: the ruling so held, but only for natural resources
An anachronism: the ruling was delivered before the shield was narrowed
An inversion: the ruling held precisely the opposite on that question
expl: The ruling rejected the proposition that private ownership alone makes a resource communal.
why: Two of the wrong options concede the proposition and qualify it, which is more tempting than a flat denial would be.
trapnote: Distinguish inversion from qualification. Here the holding is the reverse, not a narrower version.

q: A law restricting press freedom is defended as a welfare measure advancing a directive. Which statement is correct?
options: The restriction is valid, welfare being fundamental in the governance of the country
The restriction is valid if the shield is pleaded and the law is a State law
The restriction is tested against the listed grounds; a welfare label does not suffice
The restriction is void, no restriction on the press being constitutionally permissible
expl: A welfare purpose does not convert an unlisted ground into a listed one.
why: The fourth option overstates press freedom into an absolute, which is the mirror error to the State's argument.
trapnote: A purpose is not a ground. Restrictions are tested against the list, whatever the objective.

q: Children out of school are drawn into labour, and their families cannot afford litigation. Which chain correctly links the provisions?
options: Denial of schooling is a directive breach, and child labour is a policy matter alone
Denial of schooling feeds child labour, and the aid directive answers the access barrier
Child labour is a directive breach, and schooling is enforceable only after fourteen
All three limbs are directives, none being enforceable in a court of law
expl: Schooling is a right, child labour engages a right, and legal aid answers the access problem.
why: The wrong options each demote at least one limb from a right to a directive, which is the recurring error in this area.
trapnote: Trace the chain and check the category of each link. Demoting a right to a directive breaks it.

q: A statement set is accurate on duties and directives but adds that the strength of the lower House is fixed by a Fundamental Duty. Which statement is correct?
options: The added statement is defective: House strength is a structural provision, not a duty
The added statement is accurate: the duty to uphold the Constitution covers it
The added statement is defective: House strength is fixed by a Directive Principle
The added statement is accurate, the duty having been added in 2002
expl: The composition of the House is a structural provision unconnected with Part IVA.
why: The second and fourth options attempt to absorb a structural rule into a duty, which is how such defects are usually disguised.
trapnote: A correct set with one foreign item planted in it is the standard construction. Check each item's Part.

q: The November 2022 ruling on economically weaker sections is cited to deny a schooling claim. Which statement is correct?
options: The ruling extended the ceiling doctrine to educational rights generally
The ruling suspended the schooling right pending a census and delimitation
The ruling held schooling to be a directive rather than a fundamental right
The ruling concerned reservation and leaves the schooling right untouched
expl: The ruling concerned reservation and the ceiling; it did not touch the schooling right.
why: The third option borrows the census condition from a different amendment, which is a frequent cross-contamination.
trapnote: Rulings decide what was in issue. A holding cannot be exported to an unrelated right.

q: The 2024 ruling is cited to justify taking over every lodging house in a town. Which statement is correct?
options: The citation succeeds: the ruling permits takeover of all private commercial property
The citation fails: the ruling abolished the directive relied on
The citation fails: the ruling requires the resource to satisfy a community test
The citation succeeds where the State records a welfare purpose in the order
expl: The ruling imposed a test; it did not authorise indiscriminate takeover.
why: The fourth option adds a procedural fig leaf, which is how an overreaching argument is usually dressed.
trapnote: A narrowing ruling cannot support a widening argument, whatever procedural step is added.

q: The 2023 women's reservation amendment is cited as a reason to defer maternity benefits. Which statement is correct?
options: The citation succeeds: all affirmative measures await the census
The citation fails: the census condition attaches to seat reservation alone
The citation fails: the amendment repealed the maternity directive
The citation succeeds where the State has not completed delimitation
expl: The census condition governs the operation of seat reservation and nothing else.
why: The second and fourth options generalise a narrow condition, which is the standard current-affairs error.
trapnote: A condition attached to one amendment does not travel to unrelated welfare obligations.

q: The criminal procedure statute in force from July 2024 is cited in support of providing counsel to an indigent arrested person. Which statement is correct?
options: The citation is apt: the statute operationalises the legal aid directive
The citation is inapt: the statute removed the legal aid obligation
The citation is inapt: legal aid arises only at the stage of framing charges
The citation is apt only where the offence is punishable with seven years or more
expl: The statute carries forward the counsel and legal aid safeguards that give the directive effect.
why: The fourth option imports the forensic-visit threshold into an unrelated safeguard, which is a plausible cross-wiring.
trapnote: Thresholds belong to the provisions that create them. Do not carry a seven-year rule into legal aid.

q: The creation of twenty-six districts in Andhra Pradesh in 2022 is cited to claim that panchayat funds have automatically doubled. Which statement is correct?
options: The claim succeeds: funds follow the number of administrative units created
The claim fails: panchayat funding is determined by the Union finance commission
The claim succeeds where the State has accepted the finance commission report
The claim fails: devolution follows a finance commission and a budget, not reorganisation
expl: Reorganisation changes units; devolution requires a State finance commission and legislative appropriation.
why: The third option reaches the right conclusion by naming the wrong commission, which is a distinct and common confusion.
trapnote: State local bodies are funded on a State finance commission's advice, not the Union commission's.
